snippet.title: Hüma, Faysal’ın elinden son anda kurtuldu! | Sevdan Bir Ateş 9. Bölüm
snippet.description:
Sevdan Bir Ateş 9. Bölümünde;
"Hakikat"
Kızına kavuşmanın mutluluğunu yaşayan Mirza, ondan yıllarca mahrum bırakıldığı için Leyla’yı affedemez. Leyla ise geçmişte kendisine inanmayan Mirza’ya karşı boşanma kararından vazgeçmez.
Mirza, Hüma’nın kızı olduğunu artık herkese ilan eder; kurban kestirip hayırlar yaparak yıllardır özlemini çektiği babalığın sevincini yaşar. Ancak bu mutluluğun yanında büyük bir öfke de vardır. İlk DNA testinin değiştirildiğini anlayan Mirza, bunun hesabını sormak için Vuslat, Destan ve Macide’nin karşısına dikilir. Mirza’nın gerçeği kimin sakladığını bulmaya kararlı olması konakta korku yaratırken, Hüma’nın kayboluşu başta Mirza ve Leyla olmak üzere herkes için büyük bir endişeye neden olur.
Öte yandan Tespihçi ile Faysal’ın yollarının kesişmesi, Mirza’yı hiç beklemediği bir gerçeğin izine sürükler. Hüma’nın bebeğinde saklanan anahtar sayesinde gizemli bir kutuya ulaşan Mirza, içinden Leyla’nın yıllardır korktuğu silahı çıkarır. Silahı Leyla’nın önüne koyduğunda artık suskunluğun sonuna gelinmiştir. Leyla’nın sonunda anlatacağı gerçekler, Mirza’nın bugüne kadar inandığı her şeyi altüst edecek ve onu hayatının en ağır yüzleşmesine sürükleyecektir. 


Murat Ünalmış (Mirza) ile Özge Özacar’ı (Leyla) başrollerde buluşturan dizinin oyuncu kadrosunda Gökçe Eyüboğlu (Mihre), Sitare Akbaş (Destan), Taner Rumeli (Yaman), Sezin Bozacı (Macide), Yeşim Gül (Vuslat), İsmail Hakkı (Cici), Beyti Engin (İrfan), Evren Duyal (Mukaddes), Hande Canpolat (Miray), Yusuf Gökhan Atalay (Tesbihçi), Ceren Taşçı (Fidan), Aslıhan Karalar (Ceren), Yiğit Yalkın (Sefa), Dorukcan Sarıduman (Akif), Süleyman Felek (Mahmut), Azra Sare (Esma), Melih Kırkbir (Ateş), Kayra Sır (Ahu), Ege Gönülal (Yağız), Beyza Karabacak (Hüma) ve Okday Korunan (Çakır) yer alıyor. Soydan Soydaş (Faysal), Sermet Yeşil (Nasim) ve Süreyya Kilimci (Safura) ise diziye konuk oyuncu olarak eşlik ediyor.

snippet.title: 'The reason we lost is the war': JD Vance
snippet.description:
Vice President JD Vance took to social media today to deliver his post-mortem on Republicans’ grim performance in the midterms, making clear that he thought one factor deserved the most blame: “The reason we lost is the war,” Vance wrote.

Donald Trump, Jr. endorsed Vance's statement on social media shortly thereafter, writing "Every word of this."

Some observers immediately read Vance’s statement as a move to set himself up for a 2028 presidential run – but whether he has a realistic chance after last night is unclear, CNN reporters and contributors said on a panel after Vance posted his comments.

snippet.description:
Deion Sanders and Jerry Rice represent the pinnacle of their respective positions. A shutdown dynamic cornerback and a crisp route-running receiver, both considered arguably the greatest of all time at their spots. However, greatness doesn’t always look the same, and their polar-opposite personalities pushed them to the brink. Jerry was known as the no-nonsense, methodical receiver who’d rather let his game do the talking than pop his gums. Deion, however, was the flashy, loudmouth, gold-chain-rocking, multi-nickname-having, dared-to-play-two-sports counterpart. And these were all labels attached to the man also known as “Prime Time” before he officially hit the NFL!

Quick interruption to sound the alarm, but we got new Jon Bois content hot off the press: https://www.patreon.com/SecretBase/posts/history-of-our-1-174095874?utm_medium=clipboard_copy&utm_source=copyLink&utm_campaign=postshare_creator&utm_content=join_link

So when the Atlanta Falcons drafted him fifth overall in 1989 and slotted him in the same division as Jerry in the NFC West, the old guard vs. fresh blood battle immediately took shape. Whether through intense battles as division rivals, nearly coming to blows as teammates, or feelings of betrayal, the two built up a special hate for each other… AKA beef.

snippet.description:
Lo tsunami blu travolge Donald Trump e apre una resa dei conti sul peso della lobby filo-israeliana a Washington. I democratici conquistano Camera e Senato. In Texas James Talarico batte Ken Paxton, il candidato sostenuto dal presidente. In Michigan vince Abdul El-Sayed, critico del sostegno militare americano a Israele. È anche una sconfitta per l’AIPAC? A Venti alle 20, Enrica Perucchietti ne parla con Marcello Foa e l’ambasciatore Marco Carnelos, partendo dai risultati dei candidati che la lobby ha sostenuto e di quelli che ha cercato di battere. L’appoggio dell’AIPAC può ormai costare voti, soprattutto tra i democratici? Dal carovita alle promesse mancate, dal caso Epstein alla guerra in Iran, la puntata ricostruisce le ragioni della sconfitta repubblicana e i margini che restano alla Casa Bianca. Trump si dice pronto a collaborare, ma già evoca il veto. Con il nuovo Congresso, quanto spazio c’è per rivedere gli aiuti militari a Israele? E sull’Iran, Washington cercherà un accordo con Teheran o tornerà a bombardare?

snippet.title: Trump Just Lost Congress. History Says 3 Things Happen Next
snippet.description:
Trump's party lost control of Congress in the 2026 midterms. What happens next? History shows three roads presidents take after losing Congress: the veto war, the hearings, and the fight over war.

From Truman's "No comment" in 1946 to Lincoln's spot resolutions, Andrew Johnson's trial that fell one vote short and the 2019 shutdown, this film shows how each road ended before, and what to watch for now. It doesn't predict which road comes next, and it doesn't take sides.

1:12 Three Keys Congress Holds

9:09 He Has Walked All Three
10:21 Which Road Comes Next

snippet.title: The most ICONIC fall view in the US🍁 Follow americantravelarchives for more hidden gems and bucket
snippet.description:
The most ICONIC fall view in the US🍁

Follow americantravelarchives for more hidden gems and bucket list adventures across the U.S.

📍 Artist’s Bluff, Franconia Notch State Park, New Hampshire

Artist’s Bluff is one of the most famous fall views in New England, and once you’re up there you’ll see why. From the top you look down on Echo Lake with Cannon Mountain behind it, and in peak season every inch of the notch is red, orange, and gold. The hike is short, but it doesn’t feel easy.

Why it’s worth the climb:
🍂 One of the best fall foliage views in all of New England
💧 Echo Lake sits right below, surrounded by color
🏔 Cannon Mountain and Franconia Notch fill the whole view
📸 It’s one of the most photographed spots in the White Mountains
⏱ The trail is short, so you get a huge payoff without spending all day on it
⠀
Pro Tip: Get there early. This trail gets very busy in the fall, and the parking fills up fast. It’s short but steep and pretty technical, with rocks and roots most of the way, so wear real hiking shoes and take your time, especially if it’s wet.

Leave No Trace: Stay on the marked trail, pack out everything you bring, and be careful near the edge of the bluff.⠀
